subject: Post-demo recap: three recommended engines + decision factors
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-22 09:12 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: three recommended engines + decision factors

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time yesterday. Quick recap and clear next steps from our end so your team can evaluate the shortlist faster. I split the rationale into cost / latency / quality tradeoffs and included the benchmark links + prompt pack we promised.

TL;DR recommended trio (for Aurora use case):
- Redwood-RT-Medium-Quant (best latency/cost for high-throughput triage flows)
- OpenConvo-2B (balanced quality, low inference cost; good for structured extraction)
- LargeBase-13B (highest quality for clinical summarization and CPT-code mapping; higher cost)

Why these three:
- Your demo prompts highlighted two distinct patterns: many short-form triage questions (avg input 40 tokens) and fewer long summaries (avg 700 tokens). The Medium-Quant engine reduces per-token cost and keeps 95th-latency under 220ms for short requests. LargeBase-13B is the only model in our run that consistently hit your quality thresholds on the summarization prompt set (see benchmark CSV).

Deliverables attached: model_benchmarks_20281122.csv (per-engine latency/cost/ROUGE/answer-accuracy), prompt_pack_aurora_v1.md (test prompts + negative examples), and the demo recording you requested.

Next steps / asks for Aurora:
1) Confirm which two personas you want to gate: "triage" (short) and "clinical summary" (long).
2) Share any restricted PII examples we should sanitize in the eval set (if any).
3) If procurement wants an estimate: we can provide a three-tier cost projection (baseline, mid, peak) once you confirm expected qps and retention window.

I'll follow up with a concise one-page recommended rollout (canary -> A/B -> full) and a cost SLO breakdown by engine. Kimberly / Ben — adding you to coordinate pricing + procurement items.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Hi Markus — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Personas: yes, we'll formalize "triage" and "clinical summary". There is also a smaller "coding assistance" persona (extract -> CPT mapping) — do you think the LargeBase-13B covers that, or would an intermediate-sized model be better?
2) PII: we have a small set of flagged records we can share via SFTP. They contain full PHI; we will redact names but keep structure intact.
3) QPS: conservative estimate for pilot is 0.8 qps sustained with 2x peak bursts (up to 2 qps). If Redwood has per-route autoscaling, we want to see how cost scales with spikes.

One ask from procurement: can you provide a short note on SLA/uptime and any compliance certifications relevant to data-in-transit and at-rest? We'll pass to legal.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Product, Aurora Health AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-22 11:45 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: three recommended engines + decision factors

Elena — appreciate the precise asks. Short answers to your bullet list and some notes for procurement: 

- "Coding assistance" (CPT mapping): our testing indicates LargeBase-13B is the best single model for high-precision mapping to CPT categories when context length is long and you need the nuanced clinical language. If you want lower cost, an alternative is to run OpenConvo-2B for extraction then a small rule-based mapper for CPT post-processing — that combo reduces inference spend but increases engineering lift.

- Autoscaling & cost: Redwood Dedicated / Hosted both support policy-driven autoscaling. For pilot-size qps (0.8 baseline, 2 qps peak), estimates in the attached CSV show: Redwood-RT-Medium-Quant baseline ~$0.12 / 1k tokens; OpenConvo-2B ~$0.28 / 1k tokens; LargeBase-13B ~$1.40 / 1k tokens (region US-west). We can produce a scenario spreadsheet if you want per-month cost projections.

- SLA & compliance: Redwood provides 99.9% for Dedicated customers (enterprise contract). Hosted API standard SLA is 99.5% but we can include a dedicated commitment in the procurement docs. We are SOC 2 Type II in-scope for hosted control plane; for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging to meet HIPAA controls — we'll surface our compliance pack for legal as a separate attachment.

Next steps proposal (we recommend):
1) Pilot scope: run triage on Redwood-RT-Medium-Quant + coding assist experiments on LargeBase-13B (3-week eval).
2) Deliverables from Redwood: per-engine runbook, cost projection spreadsheet, compliance pack (SOC2 + HIPAA notes), and a 10-prompt regression set for each persona.
3) Technical checkpoint: schedule a 60-min workshop with your infra and security on Monday (Nov 27) to scope SFTP transfer + access model.

I'll loop in Kimberly to lock in dates and send the cost spreadsheet once we get the qps confirmation.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
